policy.principle: A blind spot is tracked until the required observer supplies the required evidence; creating a criterion or template does not resolve it.
policy.agentStopBoundary: An agent must stop before claiming human comprehension, collaborator agreement, rights clearance, deployment success, or publication approval.

blindSpots.label: Knowledge-bank depth can overwhelm editorial selection
blindSpots.risk: Archive completeness may leak into public composition and make every project appear equally important.
blindSpots.failureSignal: A grader cannot name the small proof set or explains the site as a catalog of projects.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Two independent semantic reviews of the homepage, Technical Operations page, and editorial selection register.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: Do not delete knowledge-bank records or conceal relevant work merely to reduce the public count.

blindSpots.label: One generic public may substitute for a named application audience
blindSpots.risk: A broadly accurate portfolio may not answer the operating questions of a particular hiring team.
blindSpots.failureSignal: An application packet is generic, overloaded, or cannot explain why each included case belongs.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Jamie-approved packet for one named role, followed by a target-reader review.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: An agent may draft a packet but cannot approve the role-specific selection or final submission.

blindSpots.label: LLM clarity judgments may not predict hiring-reader behavior
blindSpots.risk: Rubric-compliant prose may still fail human comprehension, trust, recall, or action.
blindSpots.failureSignal: Fewer than four of five unprimed readers identify the role, contribution, two proofs, and next action.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Five coded, unprimed 30-second reader sessions using the repository template.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: An agent may not fabricate, simulate, or relabel LLM outputs as human-reader observations.

blindSpots.label: Polished prose may substitute for decisive visible evidence
blindSpots.risk: Readers may see descriptions of proof without understanding the actual work product or embodied practice.
blindSpots.failureSignal: Priority cases rely on decorative imagery, press captures, or illegible documents instead of work-product evidence.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Rights-cleared artifact review at mobile and desktop widths with captions and evidence-scope checks.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: An agent cannot clear rights; do not publish unapproved photographs, private documents, or representative images as event-specific proof.

blindSpots.label: Recoverability may become a proxy for professional importance
blindSpots.risk: Digitally abundant campaigns may eclipse quiet facilitation, maintenance, repair, failure, or less-recorded collaboration.
blindSpots.failureSignal: Public selection tracks source volume, platform metrics, or press quantity more closely than role relevance and evidence quality.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Independent review of the archive-bias audit, public selection rationale, and open research inquiries.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: Do not invent under-recorded work, upgrade memory to corroboration, or downgrade strong evidence merely to balance the archive.

blindSpots.label: Activity and output may remain clearer than bounded consequence
blindSpots.risk: Case studies may prove effort without showing what became usable or may overreach from participation to impact.
blindSpots.failureSignal: A grader cannot distinguish Jamie's action, the output, observed use, institutional action, and collective outcome.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Two independent reviews of the outcome-language audit and priority case-study prose.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: Do not use reach, engagement, adoption, or policy causality beyond the canonical evidence relationship.

blindSpots.label: Historical range may obscure the current and future contribution
blindSpots.risk: The portfolio may read as an archive of civic and cultural history rather than evidence for present Technical Project Management and Product Operations work.
blindSpots.failureSignal: A grader can summarize past projects but cannot name the roles, environments, or next contribution Jamie is prepared for now.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Independent review of the homepage, Technical Operations page, current-fit map, and recent Source-Backed Team Memory work.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: Do not recast historical work in unsupported current terminology or imply dormant projects remain active.

blindSpots.label: Archival traces may not capture the social truth of collective work
blindSpots.risk: Role division, disagreement, credit, and consequence may remain uncertain without lived collaborator review.
blindSpots.failureSignal: A collaborator-sensitive role claim or asset is public without an explicit disposition or permission record.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Coded collaborator review outcomes and approval-register updates; private replies remain outside the repository.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: An agent cannot infer consent, pressure participation, or present an AI archival note as eyewitness testimony.

blindSpots.label: Recursive optimization may overfit the known rubric
blindSpots.risk: The portfolio can become highly compliant while an important unmodeled failure remains invisible.
blindSpots.failureSignal: No unprimed evaluator has looked for omitted problems, or holdout findings receive no disposition.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: One open-ended review by an evaluator who has not seen the criterion list, followed by materiality and deduplication review.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: An agent cannot serve as the independent human holdout; do not reveal the rubric before the open-ended pass or add every suggestion as a new criterion.

blindSpots.label: Repository depth may create disproportionate maintenance burden
blindSpots.risk: Version growth, duplicate checks, stale reviews, and competing truth stores can make safe updates too expensive for future contributors.
blindSpots.failureSignal: A new contributor cannot identify the current suite, canonical claim path, intake workflow, or release command.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Independent newcomer review of AGENTS.md, the v22 README, and the maintenance scorecard.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: Do not erase historical audit evidence or create a second canonical store in the name of simplicity.

blindSpots.label: Technical readiness may be mistaken for publication consent
blindSpots.risk: Passing checks or merging code may be treated as approval of metrics, assets, collaborator-sensitive material, contact behavior, or production launch.
blindSpots.failureSignal: An approval is missing, inferred, stale, or not tied to the reviewed commit.
blindSpots.nextEvidence: Jamie-approved launch register and, where needed, explicit collaborator or rights-holder permission.
blindSpots.stopBoundary: An agent cannot approve publication, rights, collaborator use, phone behavior, or production deployment.
